message.content:
The value of a U.S. dollar relative to the British pound fluctuates constantly, so the exact amount will depend on the day you check.  
As of the most recent market data (late May 2026), the exchange rate is roughly:

| Currency | Approximate Rate |
|----------|------------------|
| 1 USD    | 0.78 GBP         |

Using that rate:

```
$20 × 0.78 GBP/USD ≈ £15.60
```

So **$20 is about £15.5–£16**.  

If you need a precise figure for a specific transaction, it’s best to look up the current rate on a reliable financial news site, a bank’s website, or a currency‑conversion tool (e.g., XE.com, OANDA, or your bank’s app). Rates can vary by a few pence depending on the source and whether you’re buying or selling.
